summary: The article surveys efforts by local political parties and groups, from September 2023 to March 2024, to make local political leadership more diverse and inclusive. It covers mentoring programs, diversity charters, rotating leadership, youth fellowships, education workshops, allyship training, seed funding and community dialogues. It also notes ongoing underrepresentation of women and minorities and the criticism of tokenism.
one_line: Local parties launched mentoring, charter, youth, training, funding and dialogue initiatives in 2023-2024 to diversify political leadership, amid tokenism criticism.
key_facts: A report published October 15, 2023 by the Local Governance Research Collaborative (LGRC) found women and minorities remain underrepresented in key leadership positions across numerous municipalities.
Maria Gonzalez, Chairperson of the Progressive Local Leaders Initiative (PLLI), said on November 2, 2023 that "Local politics should mirror the society it serves."
The Democratic Unity Party (DUP) announced the "Open Door" program on September 29, 2023 to mentor and support candidates from underrepresented backgrounds; its architect is James Parker.
On December 1, 2023, the Neighborhood First Party (NFP) implemented a diversity charter mandating periodic reviews of leadership composition and targeted recruitment strategies.
Sarah Lee is the NFP's newly appointed Director of Inclusive Practice.
On January 10, 2024, the Regional Empowerment Coalition (REC) introduced a policy of rotating leadership roles for members of different backgrounds.
Kevin Chau, spokesperson for the Affirmative Inclusion Movement, responded to tokenism criticism on February 20, 2024, advocating a systemic shift rather than one-off appointments.
The Centrists for Change party launched the Young Leaders Fellowship on March 15, 2024 for individuals under 25, focused on engaging marginalized communities; Natasha Ramírez is Fellowship Director.
Workshops under the Grassroots Inclusivity Project (GIP), led by independent political analyst Dr. Sandra Okonkwo, began rolling out on September 21, 2023.
David Smith, a Harmonious Society Party (HSP) council member, organized allyship training sessions starting January 5, 2024.

The Fair Financing Initiative, from the Public Representation Party (PRP), launched November 12, 2023 to give seed money to prospective candidates lacking financial resources; Janet Kilmer is PRP Treasurer.
The Alliance for Inclusive Representation (AIR), founded by Richard Lam, runs community dialogues bringing local leaders and citizens together to plan a more inclusive political landscape.
